transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I, uh... I called the EAP, and they sent me here. It's just... at work, every little bang in the office makes me jump. Like, if a file drawer shuts, or someone drops a coffee mug or something. I just jump hard. And then my chest just keeps racing for... way longer than it should. It's distracting.
Are these jumps and racing heart episodes happening only when you're at work?
I... I don't really know. I guess I mostly just notice it at work. That's where it's getting in the way, so... I haven't really paid attention to whether it happens at home or not.
Do you feel anxious or on edge when you're not at work?

I guess... maybe a little? But it's mostly at work. Like... I just can't settle down there anymore. I'm always looking around... checking where my boss is, or... figuring out where the doors are. Even if I'm just trying to work with my team, I'm always kind of... watching to see if someone's coming up behind me. It's just hard to focus.
Has something upsetting or traumatic happened to you recently?
I mean... I guess you could say that. It's been about two weeks. There was this... thing with my regional boss. Late at night. That's when all this started.
Would you describe what happened with your regional boss as traumatic?
I... I don't know if I'd use that word. It was just... really bad. I'd rather not get into the details of it, if that's okay. It just... it was a really messed up night.
Have you been having any episodes where you feel an intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes?
No... not really. I mean, I get nervous, obviously, but... it doesn't suddenly spike like that. It's just more of a constant thing when I'm there. I haven't had anything like what you're saying.
Are there things or situations that you used to do or enjoy, but now avoid because of how you've been feeling?
Um... no, I don't think so. I still do the same stuff I usually do. I haven't really stopped doing anything I like, if that's what you mean.
Do you find yourself thinking about what happened with your regional boss when you don't want to?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I don't really dwell on it. It doesn't just pop into my head or anything like that. I just try to focus on my job and get through the day.
Are there any specific places, people, or things that you avoid because they remind you of what happened with your regional boss?
No... I don't avoid anything. I still go to the same places... see the same people. It's just work. I just... do my job.
Do you find that you've been having more negative thoughts about yourself or your abilities since what happened with your regional boss?
Uh, no. Not really. I mean... I know how to do my job. I don't really sit around thinking bad things about myself or... doubting what I can do. I just keep working.
Do you avoid talking or thinking about what happened with your regional boss?
I mean... it's not that I avoid it. I just... don't really have a reason to talk about it. It happened, and... that's kind of it. There's just no point in bringing it up.
Has your ability to do your job or interact with coworkers been significantly impacted by how you've been feeling?

I mean... I'm still making it to work. I'm there every day. I guess I've just been... a little slower lately. With the accounts, and... making staffing decisions. 

I've had to, uh, ask my team to double-check a few things for me. Things I normally just handle on my own. It's just... with performance reviews coming up, I'm kind of worried that these mistakes might affect my job. But I'm still working.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with coworkers or supervisors since you started feeling this way?
No, not really. I mean... I still talk to my team. We get the work done. I guess I'm just... keeping my head down a bit more. But no real problems, no.
Do you feel an overwhelming sense of fear or anxiety when you see or think about your regional boss?
I wouldn't call it... overwhelming, no. I mean, I'd rather not run into him if I can help it. But I'm not... panicking or anything like that. I just try to focus on my own work.
Do you feel anxious when you think about your regional boss?
Not really... I just prefer to keep my distance. It's not a big deal.
Have you been thinking that you're worthless or inadequate since the incident with your regional boss?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I know I can do my job. I just... I don't know, I just try to do what I need to do and go home. I haven't really been thinking about myself like that.
Have you been having thoughts that you're a failure since the incident with your regional boss?
No, not really. I mean, like I said, I know I'm good at my job. I just... I haven't been thinking about it like that.
Do you think your reactions to the noise and your behavior at work are excessive compared to what others might experience in the same situation?
I don't know... I haven't really thought about what other people would do. I just react how I react, I guess.
Do you think your reactions and feelings are directly related to what happened with your regional boss?

I mean... I'm not really sure. I guess it could be. I haven't really sat down and tried to connect it all like that. I just know I've been on edge lately... I haven't really tried to figure out exactly why.
Do you think what happened with your regional boss is the main reason you've been feeling anxious at work?
I guess it's possible... I don't really know. I just know work has been stressful lately. I haven't really thought about it being the main reason or anything.
